front.title: Negotiated, Signed Access Agreements Between Organizations' Agents: Problem Statement and Architecture (Selo)

abstract.t:
Connecting one organization's systems to another's usually requires a connector built for that pair of systems, whether written by hand, bought from a connector catalog, or packaged as a tool server for an AI model. Connectors scale with the number of pairs, carry long- lived shared credentials, and have no verifiable link to the legal entities involved or to the terms under which access was granted.
This document describes that problem and an architecture, called Selo, that aims to reduce the need for such connectors. Agents owned by verified legal entities verify each other, negotiate a typed access agreement that both parties sign, and then execute it through a standard runtime and a gateway in front of each entity's existing API, using credentials bound to the agreement. Each entity maintains its own tested, signed mapping between its system and shared capability profiles. Selo uses existing APIs; it does not replace them.
The document states requirements and an architecture to inform discussion of whether, and where, such work belongs in the IETF. It does not specify a protocol.
